questions.text_english:
(1) Consider the career of the graphologist. He or she claims to be able to assess an individual's personality by examining the shape, size and slant of their handwriting. Many organizations employ graphologists, but should they? An argument in their favour is that handwriting is an expression of our aesthetic and imaginative sense, and should therefore provide clues to personality. But in an extensive review of more than 200 studies, graphology was unable to predict any personality trait. A comparison between the results of a graphology survey and a standard personality test showed that there was no correlation. Another comparison between the analysis of graphologists and that of a control group (who knew nothing about graphology) was made. The control group, which made its assessments based on what the script said rather than how it was written, was found to be just as accurate as the graphologists. It concluded that graphology is not a reliable science.

(2) This is not to say that handwriting analysis has no place in forensics, where the expert compares two or more pieces of writing to determine whether they were written by the same person. This can prove to be vital, for example, in determining if a signature on a will is genuine. In such cases, the expert is comparing writing style, and not assessing personality.

(3) Another questionable practice is that of lie detection. The polygraph test is based on the premise that when we tell a lie, our fear of being caught causes certain physiological changes like sweating, faster heart rate and increased blood pressure. During a polygraph test, the subject is asked a series of control questions (e.g., about their name, date of birth, etc.) to establish a baseline of physiological responses. Then they are asked the relevant questions. If the physiological changes are greater when answering the relevant questions, the subject is assumed to be lying.

(4) However, it is not possible to establish a definitive baseline. Physiological changes can be caused by anxiety and fear itself. Thus, an honest person who is nervous may appear to be lying, while a cool-headed liar may pass the test. A review by the National Academy of Sciences (USA) in 2003 concluded that polygraph tests are not accurate. Furthermore, polygraph testing was found to be biased against truthful people, as they were more likely to believe the test was accurate and, therefore, more likely to feel nervous when answering relevant questions. This bias was not observed in liars, who knew the test was fallible and were, therefore, more comfortable with it.

(5) The results of these questionable practices have important implications, especially when they are used as basis for decisions. They should be evaluated critically and with healthy dose of skepticism.
questions.instruction_line_english: Based on your understanding of the text, answer the following questions :

sub_questions.text_english: What is the function of the polygraph test?
sub_questions.solution: Reference paragraph 3. The primary function of the polygraph test is lie detection.

sub_questions.text_english: State ONE ground on which graphology is considered questionable.

key_points: No correlation with standard personality test
Control group equally accurate as graphologists

sub_questions.solution: Reference paragraph 1. A primary reason graphology is considered questionable is that it is unable to predict any personality trait, as proven by extensive studies, where it showed no correlation with standard personality tests and performed no better than a control group with no training.

sub_questions.text_english: How is the polygraph test conducted?
sub_questions.solution: Reference paragraph 3. During a polygraph test, the subject is first asked a series of control questions to establish a baseline of physiological responses. Then, relevant questions are asked, and if the physiological changes are greater, the subject is assumed to be lying.

sub_questions.text_english: Polygraph tests were found to be biased against truthful people because

options_english.A: they were more likely to believe the test was accurate.
options_english.B: physiological changes can be caused by anxiety and fear.
options_english.C: they were more likely to feel comfortable when answering relevant questions.
options_english.D: a cool-headed liar may pass the test.

sub_questions.solution: Reference paragraph 4. Option A is correct as truthful people are more likely to believe the test works, causing them to feel nervous and fail.

sub_questions.text_english: Which word in paragraph (1) means the same as 'slant'?
sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct. Paragraph 1 discusses 'the shape, size and slant of their handwriting'. The word 'slant' is used as a synonym for 'slope'.

sub_questions.text_english:
State TRUE or FALSE.
The handwriting analysis has a place in forensics.
sub_questions.solution: True. Paragraph 2 explicitly states, 'This is not to say that handwriting analysis has no place in forensics...'. Its function in this field is to compare style, not assess personality.

questions.text_english:
(1) Sunlight is the source of all energy, but its rays also contain harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which is responsible for some harmful effects on the skin. This harmful radiation is subdivided according to wavelength: UVA (longest, 320-400 nm), UVB (medium, 290-320 nm), and UVC (shortest, 100-290 nm). Though UVC has the highest energy and is potentially the most dangerous, it is completely absorbed by the ozone layer and does not reach the earth's surface. However, both UVA and UVB rays are able to penetrate the atmosphere and can be harmful.

(2) Sunscreen is a topically applied product that protects the skin from the negative effects of UV radiation by absorbing, scattering or reflecting it. Effective broad-spectrum sunscreens provide protection against both UVA and UVB rays.

(3) The Sun Protection Factor (SPF) value on sunscreens is a measure of the protection against UVB radiation, which is the main cause of sunburn. The SPF value indicates how much longer it will take for skin exposed to UVB rays to turn red, compared with the same skin without protection. So, an SPF 15 sunscreen allows one to stay out in the sun 15 times longer before starting to burn. However, SPF is not a linear measure of protection: SPF 15 blocks about 93% of UVB rays, while SPF 30 blocks about 97%.

(4) Sunscreen use can reduce the incidence of some types of skin cancer. However, it cannot completely eliminate the risk. Furthermore, some studies have even shown an increased risk of melanoma (a type of skin cancer) with sunscreen use. This may be due to a false sense of security, as people may stay out in the sun longer, or it could be due to other factors such as the ingredients in the sunscreen.

(5) More research is needed to determine the relationship between sunscreen use and the prevention of all types of skin cancer. In the meantime, it is wise to use a combination of sun protection methods: limit sun exposure especially during peak hours (10 am to 4 pm), wear protective clothing and use a broad-spectrum sunscreen with an SPF 15 or higher. As the saying goes, 'an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.'
questions.instruction_line_english: Based on your understanding of the text, answer the following questions :

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the type of UV radiation which is most potentially dangerous, but does not reach the earth's surface.
sub_questions.solution: Reference paragraph 1. The most potentially dangerous form of UV radiation is UVC, which has the highest energy but is completely absorbed by the ozone layer.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the role of 'ozone layer' with respect to sunlight.

key_points: prevents dangerous UVC from reaching earth's surface

sub_questions.solution: Reference paragraph 1. The ozone layer plays a crucial role by absorbing all of the shortest and highest-energy ultraviolet radiation, known as UVC. By doing so, it prevents this most potentially dangerous form of UV radiation from reaching the earth's surface.

sub_questions.text_english: Infer from the given statement: 'SPF is not a linear measure of protection.'

key_points: Blocks different percentage of rays than implied
double SPF does not mean double protection

sub_questions.solution: Reference paragraph 3. The statement implies that doubling the SPF value on a sunscreen does not double the level of protection. For instance, SPF 15 blocks approximately 93% of UVB rays, while SPF 30 blocks about 97%.

sub_questions.text_english: A 'False sense of security' means

options_english.A: to feel secure even if you are in danger.
options_english.B: to know that you are secure and there is no danger.
options_english.C: to feel insecure when there is no danger.

sub_questions.solution: Option A is correct. Paragraph 4 mentions a 'false sense of security' where people believe themselves to be safe from harm simply because they are using sunscreen.

sub_questions.text_english: A quote, 'an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure', means

options_english.A: to understand the value of prevention is difficult.
options_english.C: to prevent a disease, we need cure.
options_english.D: prevention and cure are equally valuable.

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. In paragraph 5, this quote is used to emphasize that taking small preventative steps is much easier than trying to cure the problems that may arise.

sub_questions.text_english: Which word in paragraph (4) means the same as 'remove'?
sub_questions.solution: Option A is correct. Paragraph 4 discusses whether sunscreen can 'completely eliminate the risk' of skin cancer.

questions.text: Attempt ANY TEN from (A)-(L) of twelfth of the following tasks, as directed :
questions.text_english: Attempt ANY TEN from (A)-(L) of twelfth of the following tasks, as directed :

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete an school seminar invite.
We are delighted to invite you to a seminar on 'Acoustic Fatigue' where we _______ explore the effects of noise pollution.
sub_questions.solution: Option A is correct. A formal seminar invite uses 'shall' to express a future plan or intention.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the conversation between a doctor and his patient. Complete the sentence by reporting the patient's reply correctly.
Doctor: How do you feel now?
Patient: I am not feeling well today.
The doctor asked the patient how he felt then. The patient replied that _______.

fill_values: he was not feeling well that day

sub_questions.solution: The patient stated 'I am not feeling well today'. When reporting this, 'I' changes to 'he', 'am not feeling' backshifts to 'was not feeling', and 'today' changes to 'that day'.

sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the error and supply the correction for the following note from a school diary:
Every students must wear the id-card within the school premises.
Use the given format for your response.
Error | Correction
sub_questions.solution: The determiner 'Every' is always followed by a singular countable noun. Therefore, 'students' is incorrect and must be changed to 'student'.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the following dialogue and report it correctly:
Sam: I need to go to the grocery store.
Rita: I will go with you.
Sam told Rita that he needed to go to the grocery store, and Rita assured him that _______.
sub_questions.solution: Rita said 'I will go with you'. For reported speech: 'I' changes to 'she', 'will' backshifts to 'would', and 'you' changes to 'him'.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete a sign board on a busy road:
Drive slowly _______ you want to cause an accident.
sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. 'Unless' means 'except if'.

sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the error and supply the correction for the following line from a history journal:
The first English factories were set on the banks of the river Hugli.
Use the given format for your response.
Error | Correction
sub_questions.solution: The correct phrasal verb is 'set up', which means to establish or build.

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the correct option to fill in the blank for the given line from a travel magazine:
The experience of climbing the mountain was utterly _______.
sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct. The word needs to be an adjective describing the *experience*. 'Exhilarating' is the correct form.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete a sentence about an incident:
While the family _______ sleeping, a thief entered their house.
sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. Past continuous tense is needed for the ongoing action.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the conversation between a husband and wife. Report the husband's question correctly.
Husband: Where is my black shirt?
Wife: I sent it to the laundry.
The husband asked his wife _______.
sub_questions.solution: In reported Wh-questions, the Wh-word is retained, structure becomes assertive, pronouns and tenses change.

sub_questions.text_english:
Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option, to complete a public health awareness message.
The vaccine can significantly eliminate the _______ of infection.
sub_questions.solution: Option A is correct. Vaccines reduce the 'risk' of infection.

sub_questions.text_english:
Supply the correction for the following dialogue:
Passenger: Is the train delayed?
Clerk: No, it arrive at its scheduled time.
Use the given format for your response.
Error | Correction
sub_questions.solution: The base form 'arrive' is incorrect. Use 'arrives' (present) or 'will arrive' (future).

sub_questions.text_english:
Identify the error and supply the correction for the following line from a news report:
A recent study has found that regular exercise can improved cognitive function in older adults.
Use the given format for your response.
Error | Correction
sub_questions.solution: After modal 'can', base form 'improve' is required.

questions.text: 4. Attempt ANY ONE from (A) and (B) given below :
questions.text_english: 4. Attempt ANY ONE from (A) and (B) given below :

sub_questions.text_english: (A) You are Rajesh / Rama, a resident of Sector 14, R.K. Puram. A public park in your locality is lying in a state of utter neglect. Write a letter to the Municipal Commissioner, in about 100-120 words, drawing his attention to the poor condition of the park and requesting him to take appropriate action to restore it to its original beauty.

key_points: Format: sender address, date, receiver address, subject, salutation, body paras 1-3, closing, signature
Opening - state purpose clearly regarding park condition
Details - mention specifics like overgrown grass, broken benches, garbage
Closing - request swift action and regular maintenance

sub_questions.solution:
Rajesh / Rama
Sector 14, R.K. Puram
New Delhi
[Current Date]
The Municipal Commissioner
Municipal Corporation of Delhi
New Delhi

Subject: State of Utter Neglect of Public Park in Sector 14, R.K. Puram

Sir,

I am Rajesh / Rama, a resident of Sector 14, writing to draw your urgent attention to the deplorable condition of the public park in our locality. Once a vibrant space for all, it is now lying in a state of complete neglect.

The park has become unusable for residents. The grass is overgrown, garbage is accumulated everywhere, benches are broken, and the once beautiful landscaping is destroyed. Furthermore, it has become a haven for anti-social elements after dark due to broken lights.

I request you to kindly take immediate appropriate action for its renovation, including cleaning, repairs, and landscaping. Regular maintenance should be ensured to restore its original beauty for the benefit of our community. Thanking you.

Yours faithfully,
[Signature]
Rajesh / Rama

sub_questions.text_english: (B) You are Anita / Anish. You are keen to join a course in fashion design, after class 10. Write a letter to the Director, National Institute of Fashion Design, R.K. Puram, in about 100-120 words, making inquiries about the courses, eligibility, fee structure, hostel facilities and placement opportunities.

key_points: Format: sender address, date, receiver address, subject, salutation, body paras 1-3, closing, signature
Opening - state purpose clearly and expression of interest in fashion design
Questions - list specifics (course eligibility, fee structure, hostel, placements)
Closing - request prospectus or detailed brochure

sub_questions.solution:
Anita / Anish
[Your Address]
New Delhi
[Current Date]
The Director
National Institute of Fashion Design
R.K. Puram, New Delhi

Subject: Inquiry Regarding Fashion Design Courses after Class 10

Sir,

I am Anish, currently in class 10, with a strong keen interest in fashion design. I wish to pursue a career in this creative field immediately after completing my board exams.

I am writing to inquire about the various fashion design courses offered by your prestigious institute specifically suitable for candidates with my qualification. Kindly provide detailed information regarding the list of certificate/diploma courses, the eligibility criteria for a class 10 pass, detailed fee structure, and course duration.

Additionally, I would appreciate details on the availability of hostel facilities for outstation students and the institute's campus placement record. If a prospectus is available, kindly let me know how I can obtain one. Thanking you.

Yours faithfully,
[Signature]
Anish

questions.text: 5. Attempt ANY ONE from (A) and (B) given below :
questions.text_english: 5. Attempt ANY ONE from (A) and (B) given below :

sub_questions.text_english:
(A) The bar chart below shows the preference of students of age group 7-17 years for different types of musical instruments they want to learn.
Write an analytical paragraph in 100-120 words, analyzing the information in the bar chart.

key_points: Intro: summarize chart (musical instrument preferences of students aged 7-17)
Highest preference: focus on dominance of Guitar and Piano
Mid-range preference: focus on middle tier like Drums and Violin
Conclusion: general trend towards popular or dynamic instruments

sub_questions.solution: The bar chart illustrates the preferences of students aged 7-17 years regarding the specific musical instruments they are eager to learn. According to the data, the Guitar emerges as the most popular choice, chosen by approximately fifty students. It is followed closely by the Piano, which interests around forty-five students. Moderate interest is shown in learning dynamic and classical instruments, with roughly thirty-five students opting for Drums and thirty for the Violin. The Flute is the least popular choice among this age group, selected by only twenty students. In conclusion, students show a pronounced preference for popular, dynamic instruments like the Guitar and Piano over traditional wind instruments like the Flute.

sub_questions.text_english:
(B) You are a special correspondent for a local daily. You went to observe a mock drill organized by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) in a residential colony. Several stakeholders like resident welfare associations, fire and police departments and medical services participated in it. Use the clues given below to write a report in about 100-120 words on the mock drill event.
Clues:
Mock Drill - create awareness - residential area - fire safety - handling earthquake situation – first aid training - active participation - very successful - appreciated by all residents.

key_points: Objective - state purpose to create awareness in residential areas
Specifics - focus on fire safety, earthquake handling, first aid
Outcome - describe active participation and success

sub_questions.solution:
TITLE: NDMA CONDUCTS SUCCESSFUL MOCK DISASTER DRILL
BYLINE: By Anish/Anu Special Correspondent
[PLACE], [Current Date]: A comprehensive mock drill was organized yesterday by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) in the [Colony Name] residential colony. The primary objective was to create crucial public awareness about effective disaster management within residential areas.

The exercise witnessed active participation from several key stakeholders, including the Resident Welfare Association, fire department, police department, and medical services. The drill focused on demonstrating fire safety procedures, simulated a critical earthquake situation, and provided invaluable first aid training to the residents. All residents appreciated the unique opportunity to learn life-saving skills from experts, describing the event as highly informative and very successful in preparing the community for emergencies.

questions.text: 6. Read the following extracts and answer the questions for ANY ONE of the two given :
questions.text_english: 6. Read the following extracts and answer the questions for ANY ONE of the two given :

sub_questions.text_english:
(A) "The baker and his family never starved. He, his family and his servants always looked happy and prosperous. Their plump physique was an open testimony to this. Even today, any person with a jackfruit-like physical appearance is easily compared to a baker."
(Glimpses of India)
sub_questions.solution: Passage-based question set from option A. Answers are provided in sub_questions i-iv.

sub_questions.text_english: What can you infer about the baker's life in the past?

options_english.D: Baking was not a respected profession.

sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct. The text directly states that the baker and his family "never starved" and always looked "happy and prosperous," which is evidence that baking was a profitable profession.

sub_questions.text_english: Which evidence supports the prosperous life of the baker?
sub_questions.solution: Reference Glimpses of India (A Baker from Goa). The extract mentions that 'their plump physique' was an 'open testimony' to the fact that they always looked happy, prosperous, and never starved.

sub_questions.text_english: The comparison of a person with a jackfruit-like appearance to a baker is an example of _______.
sub_questions.solution: Option C is correct. The phrase functions idiomatically in common usage.

sub_questions.text_english: Which word in the extract means 'public statement'?
sub_questions.solution: Reference Glimpses of India (A Baker from Goa). In the given extract, the word "testimony" means 'public statement' or proof.

sub_questions.text_english:
(B) All through the night, Lencho thought only of his one hope: the help of God, whose eyes, as he had been instructed, see everything, even what is deep in one's conscience. Lencho was an ox of a man, working like an animal in the fields, but still he knew how to write. The following Sunday, at daybreak, he began to write a letter which he himself would carry to town and place in the mail. It was nothing less than a letter to God.
(A Letter to God)
sub_questions.solution: Passage-based question set from option B. Answers are provided in sub_questions v-viii.

sub_questions.text_english: What was Lencho's only hope?
sub_questions.solution: Reference A Letter to God (Lencho). According to the extract, Lencho's singular hope was "the help of God".

sub_questions.text_english: Lencho was an "ox of a man" means _______.

options_english.B: he was very strong and hardworking.
options_english.D: he was very simple and innocent.

sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. The metaphor is explained by him working like an animal in the fields.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe Lencho's faith in God.
sub_questions.solution: Reference A Letter to God (Lencho). Lencho had an immense, unshakable faith in God. He believed God's eyes see everything and wrote a literal letter asking for help.

sub_questions.text_english: Which word in the extract means 'the inner sense of right and wrong'?
sub_questions.solution: Reference A Letter to God (Lencho). The word "conscience" means 'the inner sense of right and wrong'.

questions.text: 7. Read the following extracts and answer the questions for ANY ONE of the two given :
questions.text_english: 7. Read the following extracts and answer the questions for ANY ONE of the two given :

sub_questions.text_english:
(A) I am an orphan, roaming the street.
I pattern soft dust with my hushed, bare feet.
The silence is golden, the freedom is sweet.
(Amanda!)
sub_questions.solution: Poetry-based question set from option A. Answers are provided in sub_questions i-iv.

sub_questions.text_english: What is Amanda's state of mind?
sub_questions.solution: Reference Robin Klein's Amanda!. Amanda's state of mind is troubled and stressed due to constant maternal nagging. She seeks escape through daydreaming.

sub_questions.text_english: What did she want to do as an orphan?
sub_questions.solution: Reference Robin Klein's Amanda!. She wanted to roam the streets freely, making patterns in soft dust with her bare feet.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does she call the silence golden and freedom sweet?

key_points: silence is golden: precious/valuable because mother makes too much noise
freedom is sweet: highly desirable/enjoyable because mother has restricted her

sub_questions.solution: Reference Robin Klein's Amanda!. Silence is precious due to constant nagging, and freedom is desirable due to restrictions.

sub_questions.text_english: The figure of speech used in "I pattern soft dust" is _______.
sub_questions.solution: Option B is correct. It is a metaphor describing her fantasy action.

sub_questions.text_english:
(B) Believing that they had seen
A wild and terrifying thing,
No one came near to where she lay,
A tiny speck on that white sand.
(The Trees)
sub_questions.solution: Poetry-based question set from option B. Answers are provided in sub_questions v-viii.

sub_questions.text_english: What did 'they' see?
sub_questions.solution: Reference Adrienne Rich's The Trees. 'They' saw the speaker as a wild and terrifying thing.

sub_questions.text_english: Why did no one come near 'her'?

key_points: they believed she was a 'wild and terrifying thing'

sub_questions.solution: Reference Adrienne Rich's The Trees. They were terrified because they believed she was wild and terrifying.

sub_questions.text_english: Who is 'she' mentioned in the extract?
sub_questions.solution: Reference Adrienne Rich's The Trees. 'She' refers to the speaker/poet.

sub_questions.text_english: Which word in the extract means 'scary'?
sub_questions.solution: Reference Adrienne Rich's The Trees. The word "terrifying" means 'scary'.

questions.text: Answer ANY FOUR of the following five questions, in about 40-50 words each :
questions.text_english: Answer ANY FOUR of the following five questions, in about 40-50 words each :

sub_questions.text_english: (i) Why did Valli save every coin that came her way? (Madam Rides the Bus)

key_points: wanted to take her first bus ride
needed to save 60 paise for the fare
saved money by resisting small temptations

sub_questions.solution: Reference Madam Rides the Bus (Valli). Valli saved every coin because she wanted to fulfill her dream of riding the bus to town. She needed sixty paise and resisted temptations to achieve her goal.

sub_questions.text_english: (ii) Do you think Chubukov is a good father? Give reasons for your answer. (The Proposal)

key_points: prioritized family wealth/status over daughter's happiness

sub_questions.solution: Reference The Proposal (Chubukov/Natalya). No, Chubukov is more opportunistic than a good father. He prioritizes wealth and status over Natalya's happiness.

sub_questions.text_english: (iii) What did Kisa Gotami ask Lord Buddha? What was his reply? (The Sermon at Benares)

key_points: she asked Buddha for medicine to bring her dead son back to life
Buddha replied by asking her to bring a handful of mustard seeds

sub_questions.solution: Reference The Sermon at Benares (Kisa Gotami). Kisa Gotami asked for medicine to revive her son. Buddha asked her to bring mustard seeds from a house where death had never occurred.

sub_questions.text_english: (iv) Why do the poet's eyes get full in the poem "The Fog"?
sub_questions.solution: Reference The Fog (W.H. Davies). The poet's eyes fill with tears due to sympathy for the blind man who confidently helps him despite his disability.

sub_questions.text_english: (v) Describe Amanda's life as a mermaid as visualized by Robin Klein.

key_points: in a vast, languid emerald sea

sub_questions.solution: Reference Robin Klein's Amanda!. Amanda imagines herself as a mermaid in a vast, calm emerald sea, drifting peacefully as the sole inhabitant.

questions.text: Answer ANY TWO of the following three questions, in about 40-50 words each :
questions.text_english: Answer ANY TWO of the following three questions, in about 40-50 words each :

sub_questions.text_english: (i) What did Griffin do in the house of the clergyman? (Footprints without Feet)
sub_questions.solution: Reference Footprints without Feet (Griffin). Griffin invisibly entered the clergyman's house and stole money from the desk. The clergyman and wife heard him but couldn't see him.

sub_questions.text_english: (ii) What were the reasons for Matilda's unhappiness? (The Necklace)

key_points: born into a family of clerks

sub_questions.solution: Reference The Necklace (Matilda). Matilda was unhappy because she was born into a simple family and married an ordinary clerk, yet believed she deserved luxuries, leading to constant dissatisfaction.

sub_questions.text_english: (iii) Draw a character sketch of Hari Singh. (The Thief's Story)
sub_questions.solution: Reference The Thief's Story (Hari Singh). Hari Singh is a 15-year-old experienced thief who is shrewd and cunning but transforms after experiencing Anil's trust and education.

questions.text: 10. Attempt ANY ONE of the following two questions, in about 100-120 words :
questions.text_english: 10. Attempt ANY ONE of the following two questions, in about 100-120 words :

sub_questions.text_english: (A) "The Sermon at Benares" and "For Anne Gregory", deal with the themes of 'love' and 'life'. Discuss. (100-120 words)

key_points: Intro: both texts challenge superficial attachments
Sermon: universality of death and acceptance
For Anne Gregory: superficial love based on beauty
Conclusion: need for deeper spiritual understanding

sub_questions.solution: Both "The Sermon at Benares" and "For Anne Gregory" deal with profound themes of life and love. In the Sermon, Buddha teaches Kisa Gotami about the inevitability of death, urging acceptance. In "For Anne Gregory", Yeats shows how love is often superficial, based on physical beauty (yellow hair) rather than inner worth. Both texts encourage transcending material and physical attachments to attain deeper understanding of life and true love.

sub_questions.text_english: (B) Describe the different points in Valli's bus journey and how it opened up her thinking, based on "Madam Rides the Bus". (100-120 words)

key_points: Return journey: contrast of life and death (cow)

sub_questions.solution: Valli's bus journey was transformative. On the way to town, she was excited and observant, feeling independent. In town, she showed maturity by resisting temptations. On the return, seeing the same cow dead that she had seen running joyfully earlier opened her eyes to the realities of life and death. This contrast matured her thinking significantly.

questions.text: 11. Attempt ANY ONE of the following two questions, in about 100-120 words :
questions.text_english: 11. Attempt ANY ONE of the following two questions, in about 100-120 words :

sub_questions.text_english: (A) "Trust is a very delicate thing." Discuss how trust was made and broken in context of "The Thief's Story". (100-120 words)

key_points: Anil builds trust by teaching and giving responsibility
Anil's continued trust leads to Hari's transformation

sub_questions.solution: In "The Thief's Story", trust is shown as delicate yet powerful. Anil builds trust by employing Hari, teaching him to read and write, and giving him money. Hari initially breaks this trust by stealing the money. However, Anil's continued faith in him, even after knowing about the theft, leads Hari to return the money and choose a better path. This shows that trust, though fragile, can be a catalyst for positive change.

sub_questions.text_english: (B) Griffin's brilliant discovery of invisibility was not supported by his actions. "Power should not be used as a tool to oppress others." Justify the statement with reference to "Footprints without Feet". (100-120 words)

key_points: Griffin's discovery was brilliant but misused

sub_questions.solution: In "Footprints without Feet", Griffin discovers invisibility but uses it selfishly for theft and violence. Instead of benefiting humanity, he becomes a lawless terror, robbing and assaulting people. His actions justify the statement that power should not be used to oppress others. Without moral responsibility, even a great scientific discovery becomes dangerous.
